abstract_summary: 3D scene graphs support language-guided navigation by organizing physical entities and their containment and spatial relations into hierarchical maps. Building such structured maps requires a scene representation that consistently distinguishes semantic regions and object instances across viewpoints. To this end, we...

evidence.excerpt:
Gaussian
representation learning with hierarchical 3D scene graph con-
struction. PanoGraphGS jointly learns semantic and instance
features anchored to shared Gaussian geometry. The semantic
branch combines residual feature projection and category
prototypes with confidence-weighted supervision, while the
instance branch associates view-local pseudo-labels with
persistent Gaussian instance identities to ensure consistent
object correspondence across views. As illustrated in Fig. 1,
the resulting panoptic Gaussian representation supports both
panoptic segmentation and direct Gaussian-level decoding.
The semantic-aware hierarchical reasoning module combines
structural semantics with Gaussian geometry to recover the
floor-room-stuff-objecthierarchy and its containment and
spatial relations, enabling structured spatial queries such as
locating the bed1 in the living room on floor1. CLIP

support floor-room recognition, they are
evaluated only at the object level. For KeySG, HOV-SG,
and PanoGraphGS, floor, room, and object recognition are
manually verified under a hierarchical criterion: a room is
correct only when its floor and room identities and semantic
category are correctly identified, while an object is correct
only when its floor, room, and object identities are all correct.
Panoptic segmentation is evaluated using mIoU for region
overlap and mBIoU for object and structural boundaries. For
instance-only methods such as Unified-Lift, these metrics
are computed after per-image optimal instance matching
without semantic categories. For panoptic methods, including
PanopticRecon++ and PanoGraphGS, a match is correct
only when both instance identity and semantic category are
correctly predicted, yielding a stricter criterion.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript reports evaluation against external benchmark ground-truth annotations on ScanNet++, Replica, and NaviGS for panoptic segmentation metrics, and manually verified hierarchical ground truth for scene graph accuracy.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External benchmark ground-truth annotations for 2D panoptic segmentation (mIoU, mBIoU) and manually verified hierarchical ground truth for 3D scene graph accuracy.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: SAM3-generated 2D pseudo-segmentation masks combined with photometric RGB losses and confidence-weighted contrastive/prototype losses.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical improvements in hierarchical accuracy and panoptic boundary quality align with the proposed joint 2D-3D representations and association mechanisms [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0021, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0027, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0036].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is evaluated against established baselines (HOV-SG, ConceptGraphs, Unified-Lift, PanopticRecon++) across three datasets (ScanNet++, Replica, NaviGS) on 2D panoptic segmentation (mIoU, mBIoU) and 3D scene graph identification accuracy, supported by an ablation study [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0021, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0027, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0036].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard external ground-truth masks and annotations on ScanNet++, Replica, and NaviGS are used to compute mIoU/mBIoU and scene graph accuracy [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0030, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0031].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard ground-truth benchmark annotations for 2D panoptic segmentation (mIoU, mBIoU) and manually verified hierarchical ground truth for 3D scene graph accuracy [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0030, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0031].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: SAM3-generated 2D pseudo-segmentation masks combined with photometric RGB losses and confidence-weighted contrastive/prototype losses [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0013, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0019, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0022].

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge limitations, including poor room boundary delineation in open-plan spaces (e.g., open kitchens) and the offline nature of the scene graph construction [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0040].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the shared rendering formulations, residual projection MLP for prototype semantics, Hungarian matching for view-consistent global instance assignment, confidence weighting, and hierarchical rule-based graph construction from structural Gaussians [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0015, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0016, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0018, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0020, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0025, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0027].
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents a coherent technical framework, solid algorithmic details, clear baselines, rigorous ablation analysis, and appropriate limitations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript proposes PanoGraphGS, an approach combining 3D Gaussian Splatting with prototype-based semantic learning and Hungarian association-based instance learning, together with a semantic-aware floor-room-stuff-object scene graph construction pipeline and a new benchmark dataset NaviGS [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0002, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0008, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0018, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0025].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper presents a coherent technical framework, solid algorithmic details, clear baselines, rigorous ablation analysis, and appropriate limitations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge limitations, including poor room boundary delineation in open-plan spaces (e.g., open kitchens) and the offline nature of the scene graph construction [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0040].
